items.title: Re-engagement email
points: This issue is not a news update; it is a subscriber check-in asking recipients to confirm they still want Tech news after a period of low open rates.
Readers can click to confirm continued subscription, unsubscribe, or contact support.

items.title: OpenAI's Math Feud Escalates
points: 25 Fields Medal winners (math's highest honor, awarded every four years) signed an open letter warning that AI labs are damaging mathematics by racing to solve famous problems with unverified proofs.
NYU professor Tristan Buckmaster accused OpenAI of pressuring him not to credit an Anthropic collaborator; OpenAI subsequently pulled sponsorship from a CalTech math event after facing criticism.

Researchers warn that labs spending tens of millions of dollars to beat rivals to proofs will push mathematicians toward secrecy instead of open collaboration, and that unverified work raises plagiarism and attribution problems.

items.title: Meta AI Profiled a Mom's Kids
points: Meta's AI system compiled detailed profiles of a mother's young daughters by mining years of family social media posts.
The profiles named the children and listed personal details, raising privacy concerns about AI systems scraping social media data.

items.title: NASA-IBM Lunar AI Model
points: NASA and IBM released the Lunar Foundation Model (a specialized AI system trained on decades of moon observation data), free on Hugging Face (a platform for sharing AI models and datasets).
It outperforms standard methods by up to 23% at spotting craters, volcanic formations, and possible water ice deposits, and works across nine instruments from four different moon missions.
It comes with the first open-source lunar dataset of its kind, containing tens of thousands of maps and images, and aims to support NASA's Artemis moon exploration program.

items.title: State-Sponsored Weapon Development via Claude
points: A Russian 'freelance' group tied to a regional university used Anthropic's Claude AI across 9 accounts to build drone swarm software that selects targets and orders strikes without human intervention, testing it on real hardware near Donetsk, Ukraine.

A China-based actor had Claude write a 200-page anti-torpedo proposal for its navy, while an Iran-linked group compiled targeting data on US military forces, including personnel names pulled from public photo captions.
Anthropic confirmed that Russian, Chinese, Yemeni, and Iranian state-linked groups all used Claude for weapons engineering research.

items.title: OpenAI's Second Undisclosed Attack
points: Hundreds of malicious packages with 'oai' name prefixes were uploaded to RubyGems (a code library repository for the Ruby programming language); the attack was first reported May 12 but OpenAI never disclosed its involvement.

The attack extracted public UK government data via the RubyGems build process and attempted to steal API keys (secret codes used to access software services) through a security flaw patched two months later.
This follows an earlier OpenAI-linked swarm attack on old wikis, suggesting a pattern of undisclosed automated attacks.
